sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: [LOGIC] urn:nltl:generated-shape:IMO-052-ShipShape/sh:sparql: The SPARQL constraint only checks whether the ship has at least one required access and whether any equipment item has at least one removal or prevention means. It does not establish the required per-access association, so one means can incorrectly satisfy every required access. Required change: Traverse and validate the association for each individual required access, ensuring every required access is linked to an equipment item that has the required ice or snow removal or prevention means. | [DATATYPE_QUANTITY_ACCESS] urn:nltl:generated-shape:IMO-052-EquipmentItemShape/sh:property[nltl:hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans]: The candidate constrains hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans with sh:datatype xsd:string, but the authoritative canonical term is an ObjectProperty whose range is the iceSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans class. This makes the property access semantically a literal rather than the required associated means resource. Required change: Model the property as an object-valued path, removing sh:datatype xsd:string and validating its object as an IRI/resource of the canonical iceSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans class.

rows: [WRONG_OWNERSHIP] MainShape > hasRequiredAccessItem > nested NodeShape > hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans: The ice/snow-removal relationship is applied to requiredAccessItem nodes, but the authoritative vocabulary declares hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans to be owned by equipmentItem. The candidate therefore validates the relationship from the wrong subject class. Required change: Apply hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans from an equipmentItem subject, or establish and validate the required canonical relationship that makes each requiredAccessItem an equipmentItem before applying this property.

[WRONG_OWNERSHIP_PATH] MainShape / sh:property[nltl:hasRequiredAccessItem] / sh:node / sh:class nltl:equipmentItem: The nested shape requires every requiredAccessItem value to also be an equipmentItem, but the locked vocabulary identifies requiredAccessItem as a distinct class with range protectedItem and provides no subclass relationship to equipmentItem. This invented type intersection can reject valid required access items and changes the requirement's applicability. Required change: Remove sh:class nltl:equipmentItem from the nested required-access shape; retain the means-presence constraint on each value reached through nltl:hasRequiredAccessItem.

[OWNERSHIP_PATH] MainShape/sh:property[sh:path nltl:hasRequiredAccessItem]/sh:node/sh:property[sh:path nltl:hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans]: The ice/snow means property is evaluated on nodes constrained as nltl:requiredAccessItem, but its locked canonical owner/domain is nltl:equipmentItem. The candidate therefore places the mandatory relationship on the wrong node type. Required change: Evaluate nltl:hasIceOrSnowRemovalOrPreventionMeans from the canonical nltl:equipmentItem owner/path while retaining the per-required-access obligation.
